results.question: Which pathogen causes Rice Blast, and to which taxonomic group does it belong?
results.note: The single most converged requirement: five of six models proposed it, and all five made it their own question number one. The benchmark asks the coverage form of the same relation - how many diseases have any pathogen - never the answer form.
results.partial: v0.6 types every pathogen as rice:Pathogen and nothing more, so there is no taxonomic group to return; the closest available identity is the external alignment

queries.label: Causal pathogen of Rice Blast, with its external identity
Every disease with its causal pathogen - the answer form of benchmark CQ-01

results.question: Which vector species transmits Rice Tungro Bacilliform Virus, and by which transmission mode?
results.note: A three-hop chain: vector -> agent -> disease. Proposed by five of six models.
results.partial: transmission mode is not a property in v0.6, so the mode cannot be returned

queries.label: Vector, the agent it transmits, and the disease that agent causes

results.question: Which symptoms does Bacterial Leaf Blight produce, on which plant organ, and at which growth stage?
results.note: The diagnostic question in its plainest form.
results.partial: plant organ is not modelled in v0.6; growth stage is attached to the disease, not to the individual symptom, so the two are returned as a cross product rather than a fact

queries.label: Symptoms of Bacterial Leaf Blight, with the stages at which the disease occurs

results.question: Which diseases share symptoms with Brown Spot, and which symptoms discriminate between them?
results.note: Differential diagnosis. Proposed independently by five of the six models and absent from the benchmark, which asks only whether symptoms are attached, never which conditions they fail to separate.

queries.label: Conditions sharing at least one symptom with Brown Spot
queries.sparql:
SELECT ?other (COUNT(DISTINCT ?shared) AS ?shared_symptoms)
WHERE {
  rice:Brown_Spot rice:indicatedBy ?shared .
  ?other rice:indicatedBy ?shared .
  FILTER (?other != rice:Brown_Spot)
}
GROUP BY ?other
ORDER BY DESC(?shared_symptoms)

queries.label: Symptoms that discriminate Brown Spot from Rice Blast

results.question: Which environmental conditions are reported to favour Sheath Blight?
results.note: Proposed by a single model, and kept for exactly that reason: the questionnaire needs low-convergence CQs or the hypothesis that convergence predicts expert-rated relevance cannot be tested. It turns out to be answerable and well populated.

queries.label: Conditions that increase the risk of Sheath Blight
Every condition-to-entity risk link in the graph

results.question: At which growth stages is Brown Planthopper reported as most damaging?
results.partial: v0.6 records that a pest occurs at a stage, not how damaging it is there, so the question's ranking cannot be answered - occurrence is returned instead

queries.label: Growth stages at which Brown Planthopper occurs

results.question: Which control measures are recommended for Stem Borer, of which management category, and on which source authority?
results.note: Actionability - the KG must not diagnose what it cannot advise on. Proposed by five of six models.
results.partial: management category (chemical / biological / cultural) and source authority are not modelled in v0.6; only the treatment itself and its prerequisites can be returned

queries.label: Treatments for Stem Borer and what each requires

results.question: Which images are annotated as showing Hispa damage?
results.note: The most basic cross-modal retrieval there is. The benchmark checks that annotations are typed, never that they can be retrieved by condition.

queries.label: Images annotated as Hispa, with their retrievable URL

results.question: How is the image corpus distributed across conditions and entity types?
results.note: PARTIAL. The elicited question also asks for plant part and capture type. v0.6 models neither, so this implements the answerable half and the rest stays on the v0.7 plan. Reported as partial rather than passed.
results.partial: plant part and capture type are not modelled in v0.6

queries.label: Images per annotated condition and entity type
Images per source dataset

results.question: Which visible symptoms are annotated in a given image?
results.note: Reads the visual layer from the image side rather than the symptom side - which is what exposes how thin it is.
results.partial: only 1,442 of 10,407 images (14%) carry a captures link, and every one of them points at the same symptom

queries.label: Symptoms annotated in one image that has them
How many distinct symptoms the whole image corpus captures

results.question: Which disease or pest is best supported by the visual evidence in a given image?
results.note: The full cross-modal chain: image -> symptom it captures -> conditions that symptom indicates. The image is chosen by the query itself rather than hardcoded, so the test survives any re-import of the corpus.

queries.label: Candidate conditions for one annotated image, ranked by supporting symptoms

results.question: Which visual features separate Brown Spot from Rice Blast?
results.note: The pair the models named most often as visually confusable. Answered from the symptom layer; v0.6 has no lesion shape/colour descriptors, so the separation is by symptom identity rather than by visual feature.
results.partial: separation is by symptom, not by lesion descriptors, which v0.6 does not carry

queries.label: Symptoms unique to each of the two conditions
Symptoms the two share, which therefore cannot separate them

results.question: Which symptoms described in the literature have supporting image evidence, and which do not?
results.note: The multimodal grounding question asked as a partition rather than a ratio. Benchmark CQ-18 measures the same relation as a coverage percentage; this returns the two lists, which is a far blunter way of seeing the same thing.

queries.label: Symptoms partitioned by whether any image captures them
The symptoms with no image evidence at all

results.question: Which disease described in the literature matches the condition annotated in a given image?
results.note: Joins through the annotated class rather than through captures, so it reaches all 10,407 images instead of the 1,442 that CQ-A16 can reach. Same cross-modal claim, different and much better populated join.

queries.label: Literature evidence for the condition annotated in one image
How many images reach a literature-described condition

results.question: Which treatment does the literature prescribe for a condition identified from an image?
results.note: The full multimodal claim of the resource, end to end: an image leads to an agronomic recommendation. Proposed by a single model.

queries.label: Image -> annotated condition -> recommended treatment
How many images reach at least one treatment
